reasons: Deviation is correctly characterized: § 5.1 gives only a reasonable-care services standard plus authority/law-compliance, with no documentation-conformance warranty, no malicious code warranty and no repair/replace/refund or re-performance remedy, while p0074 puts all Materials 'AS IS' with no express-warranty carve-out — materially below the playbook position and close to walk-away.

Redline is actionable and reaches the rule's model language: adds a 90-day conformance warranty on Deliverables/Materials, a malicious code warranty, and an at-IBM's-option re-performance/repair/replacement/refund remedy, and inserts 'EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY WARRANTED IN SECTION 5.1' into the disclaimer so it no longer swallows the express warranty.

The failed 'warranty period ≥ 90 days' check is a regex false negative: the inserted text reads 'for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery', which satisfies the rule (and matches the rule's own model language and fallback for services/deliverables).
The 0.460 changed-character ratio on p0074 reflects only a short prefixed carve-out on an otherwise untouched all-caps disclaimer; that is the smallest edit that achieves the playbook position.
Comment is accurate, correctly cites §§ 5.1 and 5.4(c), states what changed and why, and offers a shorter-period fallback in the required tone.

Minor drafting nits only (not fatal): p0062's terminal period was not converted to '; and' before the new items (c)/(d), and the remedy sentence is appended inside item (d) rather than standing alone; the 'knowingly ... introduced by IBM' qualifier also slightly weakens the malicious code warranty relative to the preferred position and could be tightened in negotiation.
